solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bees do it in sun, getting quite hot

parts.note: quite hot weather is warm

explanation.surface: Bees go about their business in the sunshine on a fairly hot day.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees form a large flying cluster when they leave a hive with a new queen, a verb sense.

clue.text: Payment made by end of dispute

definitions.meaning: a payment such as a divorce or compensation award
the resolving of a quarrel by agreement

explanation.surface: A sum handed over to close a disagreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A settlement is both money paid and the agreed resolution of a dispute.

clue.text: Views expressed in debate are not admitting fix

indicators.note: admitting means the contraction takes the sticky word inside it

parts.note: are not contracts to aren't
to gum is to fix with glue

explanation.surface: Opinions aired in a discussion refuse to allow any rigging.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument is a case or reasoning put forward in a discussion.

clue.text: Smew aunt confused with another bird

indicators.note: confused means the letters are muddled up

explanation.surface: A smew, a small duck, is mistaken for a relative's other bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The mute swan is the common white swan of Britain, a species of waterbird.

clue.text: May goes round Welsh resort, we hear, with nothing on, just a set of bells

indicators.note: goes round means the word for may encircles the rest of the wordplay

parts.note: may and can both express permission

indicators.note: we hear signals that a word is to be taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: Rhyl is a seaside resort on the north coast of Wales
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone called May tours a Welsh seaside town wearing nothing but a set of bells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' makes the resort's name a sound-alike for a small stream; 'May' looks like a woman's name but is the verb of permission. 'just' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A carillon is a tuned group of church or tower bells played from a keyboard.

clue.text: Australian swimmer's first to get tailpiece

parts.note: the cod is a fish, a swimmer

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An Australian swimmer comes first to finish off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' suggests an athlete, but is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the concluding passage of a piece of music, its tail.

clue.text: Guarantee radio listener may hear near the coast

indicators.note: a radio listener hears only sound, so the phrase is identified by how it is pronounced

parts.note: inshore means close to the shore

explanation.surface: A listener tuned to the shipping forecast is promised coastal news.
explanation.definitionFit: To insure is to protect or guarantee against loss, here as a verb.

clue.text: Plate dog perhaps turned upside down

indicators.note: in a down clue turned upside down means read from the bottom up

parts.note: a dog is an example of a beast

explanation.surface: A dish knocked over by a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamina is a thin layer or plate of material, as of rock or metal.

clue.text: Exodus found in New Testament, or immediately after?

indicators.note: found in means the book abbreviation sits inside the other

parts.note: Ex is the abbreviation for the book of Exodus

explanation.surface: Is Exodus in the New Testament, or does it come straight afterwards?
explanation.walkthrough: Exodus belongs to the Old Testament, which makes the question a neat red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Next means coming straight after in order, without any gap.

clue.text: Merry Margery, flipping meanie

parts.note: merry is slang for slightly drunk, as is tight

indicators.note: flipping means the surname is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: Margery Daw is the girl in the nursery rhyme See-Saw Margery Daw

explanation.surface: Someone cheerfully complains about a stingy person named Margery, using a mild oath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' poses as a mild British oath but reverses DAW to WAD; the see-saw of the rhyme adds to the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightwad is a miser, someone mean with money, so a meanie in the stingy sense.

clue.text: A charmingly old-fashioned Conservative's brought in to advise

indicators.note: brought in means the party letter is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: quaint means attractively old-fashioned
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A quaint old Tory is called in to give advice.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquaint someone with something is to inform or advise them of it.

clue.text: Trophy on table in cabinet

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a cup is a trophy
board is an old word for a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A trophy stands on a table inside a display cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupboard is a storage cabinet with doors and shelves.

clue.text: Amount of money put up with a little being declared

parts.note: to lump it is to put up with something unwelcome

indicators.note: being declared means the word is spoken, so its sound counts

parts.note: some can mean a little, as in some sugar

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates a small sum of money being declared to the taxman.
explanation.definitionFit: A lump sum is a single payment of a whole amount at once rather than instalments.

clue.text: Grand joke by one interrupting Scotsman

indicators.note: interrupting means the pieces break into the Scottish name

parts.note: Mac is a familiar address for a Scotsman
a jest is a joke
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A big joke breaks in on a Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Majestic means stately and impressive, synonymous with grand.

clue.text: Brandy very gently poured into beer by sailor

indicators.note: poured into means the music marking goes inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
PP, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quiet playing
Jack, or Jack Tar, is a traditional name for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor carefully pours brandy into his beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Applejack is an American spirit distilled from cider, a kind of apple brandy.

clue.text: Carrying on with relative preservation of silence?

parts.note: a shop keeping goods is carrying them in stock
mum, mother, is a relative

explanation.surface: Persevering with a family member who will not speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on with' just joins the pieces; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep mum is an idiom for staying quiet, so the phrase means maintaining silence.

clue.text: Elation centred around European agreement

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Joy focused on a European pact.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'around' signals an anagram of ELATION CENTRED plus E; the French phrase means cordial understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: The Entente Cordiale was the 1904 accord between Britain and France, so an agreement.

clue.text: Ignore price reduction

definitions.meaning: an amount taken off the price

explanation.surface: Overlook a money-off offer.
explanation.definitionFit: To discount is to disregard, and a discount is a cut in price.

clue.text: Seamen in the drink

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, makes seamen ABs

explanation.surface: Sailors falling into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the drink' is slang for the sea, but here 'drink' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green aniseed-flavoured spirit.

clue.text: One causing anguish to Queen needs counsellor

parts.note: R, for Regina, is the abbreviation for queen
a mentor is a trusted adviser or counsellor

explanation.surface: A royal needs the help of an adviser because someone is distressing her.
explanation.definitionFit: A tormentor is a person who inflicts suffering, the agent noun of torment.

clue.text: Fan club?

parts.note: a fan rotates, and the ... Club is a worldwide service organisation

explanation.surface: A society of admirers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotary describes turning motion, like a fan, and names a famous club of service volunteers.

clue.text: Garden Richard's built around ornament

indicators.note: built around means the outer words enclose the letters wanted

explanation.surface: Richard's garden has been constructed around a decorative feature.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrich is to adorn or embellish, so to ornament, as a verb.

clue.text: Verdict I only can bring in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: can bring in means the letters sit inside the run of words shown

explanation.surface: Only a verdict can introduce a way of talking.
explanation.definitionFit: Diction is a person's style of enunciation and word choice, the way they speak.

clue.text: Charlie's picture replaced at a reduced rate

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: replaced means the letters are put back in a different place

explanation.surface: A man named Charlie has had his photo swapped for a cheaper one.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut-price goods are sold at a discount, below the normal cost.

clue.text: Company provided cap

parts.note: provided means if, as in provided that

explanation.surface: A firm supplied headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A coif is a close-fitting cap covering the top and sides of the head.

clue.text: Count's in advance, being cut short

indicators.note: being cut short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: early means ahead of time

explanation.surface: A nobleman arrives ahead of time but is interrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is the British rank equivalent to a continental count.

clue.text: Get used to bill coming before trade

indicators.note: coming before places the first piece ahead of the next

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
custom means trade or business from customers

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper learns to accept invoices arriving ahead of the business.
explanation.definitionFit: To accustom someone is to make them familiar with something until it is habitual.

clue.text: Machine regulator's smart turn

parts.note: fly is British slang for sharp or clever
to wheel is to turn round

explanation.surface: A clever spin on a machine control.
explanation.definitionFit: A flywheel is a heavy wheel that smooths a machine's running speed, regulating it.

clue.text: Heating unit hospital needed in time

indicators.note: needed in means the hospital letter goes inside the period word

parts.note: a term is a period of time

explanation.surface: A hospital needs heating installed in good time.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a unit of heat, used in Britain to measure gas supplied.
